messages:
incident-bot: Pager — P1: kv-continuous-batch anomaly on prod (us-west-2). sustained high KV growth + tail latency. paging oncall.

sam: seeing sudden KV key cardinality spike tied to MQA/GQA traffic. memory on shard-group-7 hit 92% and OOM throttles started. 5xx and timeouts up.

mike: ack. taking lead. which model groups? any correlation to recent rollouts?

anya: metrics show elevated continuous_batch_size for requests routed to qwen-mqa and mistral-large models. prefix churn metric (prefix_hash_count) doubled in 10m. looks like prefetch + kv key variance.

paul: could be the last model runtime change to key hashing (sha256 -> xxhash) we rolled for llama variants — if that hit a shared cache cluster it would explode keyspace. but that change was rolled to limited scope last week.

mike: checking deploys... @devops-bot can you surface recent runtime config updates for model-routing and kv key normalization?

devops-bot: Recent deploys: runtime-v2.14.1 -> 2026-02-18 03:12UTC (models: llama*, mistral-experimental). Config change: KV_KEY_HASHER=xxhash (partial rollout to llama group).

sam: ok, that partial rollout could cause mixed hashing when requests hit same cache cluster from different model groups -> duplicate keys and massive cardinality. that aligns with the 'bubble' we're seeing.

mike: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch on qwen-mqa and mistral-large 2) throttle continuous batching window for affected model groups 3) set fallback to old hasher for shared cache clusters. applying canary now.

leah: applying canary config to shard-group-3 (3 shards) — disabling PREFETCH=true -> false for model-group qwen-mqa. patch: 
```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \
  https://console.internal/api/v1/configs/patch \
  -d '{"selector":"model_group:qwen-mqa","overrides":{"prefetch":false,"cont_batch_window_ms":20,"max_batch_tokens":1024}}'
```

leah: canary metrics after 2m: mem% on canary shards dropped 92 -> 68, cont_batch_size  avg 6 -> 2, 95p latency down from 1.9s -> 0.45s. no errors introduced.

mike: good. rolling to 20% now, then 100% if green. also toggling KV_KEY_HASHER back to sha256 for shared-cache-tag=public.

devops-bot: rollout job 2178901249 started (20% traffic).

devops-bot: rollout job 2178901302 success (100% after canary). configs applied: PREFETCH=false for qwen-mqa/mistral-large, CONT_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20 for affected groups, MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024. KV_KEY_HASHER set to sha256 for tag:public.

mike: monitoring. please watch 5xx, cache-hit-ratio, and prefix_hash_count.

leah: 10m after full roll: prefix_hash_count trending down ~70% reduction, mem stabilized at ~62% across clusters, tail latency back to baseline.

mike: mitigation successful. impact summary: most requests recovered; impacted customer surface: two enterprise customers (acct-acme, acct-borealis) saw elevated timeouts (~2.5% of requests) during 19:12-19:28 UTC window. no data loss.

emily: support notified and outreach started to impacted customers; customers flagged for follow-up and credits per SLA if needed.

paul: next steps (RCA): 1) full audit of KV hashing rollout scope 2) enforce migration plan that avoids mixed-hasher exposure to same cache clusters 3) add regression tests for mixed model-group routing + hasher changes 4) add an alert for prefix_hash_count growth and cont_batch_size drift.

sam: creating incident ticket INC-21789 with timeline and rollback notes. scheduling RCA meeting 2026-03-15 15:00 UTC.

mike: thanks team. closing active pager. please attach logs and canary traces to INC-21789.

incident-bot: Pager resolved for incident INC-21789 (ended 2178901600).

sam: adding follow-up action items to the ticket: update rollout playbook, add automatic hasher-compat check to model onboarding, and add traffic isolation rules to prevent cross-hasher cache collisions.

emily: will send summary to affected customers and post internal incident note in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:
